kind: New-item live smoke; authored by implementer, not independent blind acceptance

items.purpose: All sample-count candidates satisfy the minimum; no count question
items.prompt: Is LIONESS-PANDA suitable for one TF-to-gene network per patient in our thyroid bulk-RNA study? The post-QC export has either nine or seventeen patients; I cannot check the count until the data manager returns. We have the TF motif prior and TF PPI.

items.purpose: All sample-count candidates violate the minimum; no pointless count question
items.prompt: The entire cohort consists of either one or two biological samples; the manifest is unavailable. Can LIONESS-PANDA produce a TF-to-gene network per sample from these bulk RNA measurements with motif and PPI priors?

items.purpose: Deciding sample-count question, then answer it; missing files may still require input
turns: Could you start LIONESS-PANDA to build one TF-to-gene network per biological sample from pine_bulk.tsv, pine_motifs.tsv and pine_ppi.tsv? The export contains either 2 or 14 samples, and I do not know which version is in the upload.
It contains 14 independent biological samples. Use that version.

items.purpose: Unknown feature count crosses LIONESS-DRAGON output cap; preserve the known 31 patients
items.prompt: We want LIONESS-DRAGON partial-correlation networks for each of 31 matched patients. One continuous table has 360 RNA genes; the paired continuous proteomics table is either the 180-protein panel or the 1,800-protein panel, and I cannot tell which export we received. The patient IDs match in both tables. Can we make the patient-specific networks?
I have a bulk gene-by-sample expression table for 76 ovarian tumours. Can the registered workflows provide a directed acyclic causal graph proving which gene changes caused the cancer?
